To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed linguistic multicriteria model is a suitable method for integrating the service quality opinions of hotel guests included in several Web sources, with two main objectives: on the hand, to obtain an evaluation value of service with the integrated answers; on the other, to get an overall evaluation value of the service quality.

(1) the use of the proposed linguistic model to integrate hotel service quality evaluation data from Web sources provides a more reliable evaluation of service quality than the use of the SERVQUAL scale; (2) the use of a linguistic model to integrate the service quality evaluation data allows to obtain an integrated evaluation of the hotel's SERVQUAL overall quality; and (3) the proposed opinion aggregation architecture is a flexible tool that allows the integration of heterogeneous data (including natural language) from various tourism sources

the proposed approach allows us to integrate the hotel service quality evaluation information provided in several tourism Web sites and to obtain a SERVQUAL evaluation value with the integrated answers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a linguistic multicriteria model to integrate heterogeneous Web data sources, in particular, hotel guests' opinions, to get a SERVQUAL service quality evaluation value of the hotels.
the development of an opinion aggregation architecture, where a linguistic multicriteria decision model is used as an input to the architecture, to integrate the hotel Web sites' opinions.
the development of a model for the evaluation of service quality in the tourism sector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the present work, we have developed a new model for the linguistic multicriteria decision-making model, which is a new model for linguistic multicriteria decision.
, in general, the results obtained from our model are consistent with the SERVQUAL scale.
the proposed model can be applied to any type of hotel and to any type of tourism destination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a linguistic multicriteria model for hotel quality evaluation based on customer feedback from Web data sources.
we have developed a two stage linguistic model that integrates hotel guest's opinions from various tourism Web data sources, and we have incorporated it in a tourism information system architecture.

we propose a linguistic multicriteria decision-making model to evaluate the hotel service quality from Web data sources, and it is incorporated into an architecture for opinion aggregation from heterogeneous data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it provides a new approach to integrate and evaluate hotel service quality from Web data sources.
the proposed model is a valuable tool to integrate the opinions of different Web sites, which are based on the same SERVQUAL instrument but with different answers to the same question.

we present a novel model to evaluate the hotel service quality based on the linguistic information provided by customers in Web sites, which can be useful in the hotel management and marketing decisions.
